main_text.p: justius, aut à religione magis abhorrens, quàm Divinum Christi θεανθρώπου[?] sanguinem, peccatorum omnium expiatorium, cum humana fæce peccabili, in eadem satisfactionum remuneratione commiscere. Dein, quàm ri-diculum est, eas satisfactiones negare esse duas, quarum si una sufficiens sit, alteram superfluficientem & superfatisfactoriam esse necesse est!

In Evang. Hom. 22.Hæc figmenta Adversariorum {h}Gregorius Pontifex, si nunc in vivis esset, ex animo execraretur: cujus erat hæc sancta & Divina professio; Ipsa Redemptoris nostri passio longè ipsa diversa à nostra: (nempe illa quam martyres sustinent) quoniam ipse sine culpa pertulit, quòd nos cum culpa toleramus. Quibus verbis, nec duas satisfactiones unam esse patitur; nec nostram, quæ est cum culpa, satisfactionem esse pro pœna. Ergo commeritoria vestra virtus ad consequendam vitam æternam, ex condignitate vestri operis, quæ erat Christi sanguinis pretio empta, nihil aliud est quàm Meriti Christi absolutissimi fœda conspur-catio.

page.notes: The Greek word in the first line is hard to read; the letters are approximate and marked [?]. The marginal reference mark "h" is in the margin beside the second paragraph. The bottom right shows "IIII Tua-": read as signature IIII and catchword Tua-. The text in italics (Ipsa Redemptoris ... toleramus) is partly uncertain; the word "quòd" and the repeated "ipsa" may be misread. Faint show-through text on the right side of the page was ignored.
